subject: Orchid integration: V11a p95 variance — request to activate emergency traffic split and temporary SLA carveout
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@orchid.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orchid.com
Date: 2027-12-01T08:12:45Z
Subject: Latency variance observed on Orchid integration - Model v11a

Hi Logan,

We're seeing a significant p95 latency increase on our integration since the rollout of model v11a last night. Our production p50 is fine but p95 has gone up from ~210ms to ~820ms for the last 3 hours; user complaints are starting to come in. I've attached a CSV with timestamped samples and a screenshot of the dashboard.

This affects the checkout flow for some EU users. Our SLOs require p95 < 400ms; this clearly exceeds that. Can Redwood either:
- revert traffic to the previous served variant, or
- activate a fallback split to the quantized v11a-compact variant while you investigate?

We opened a support ticket (SR-18732) and can provide more traces if needed. Please treat as urgent.

Thanks,
Maria Santos
Technical Product Manager, Orchid Labs
Maria.Santos@orchid.com
+44 20 7946 0XXX

Attachments: orchid_latency_samples_20271201.csv (text/csv), orchid_p95_dashboard_screenshot.png (image/png), support_ticket_SR-18732.pdf (application/pdf)

Subject: Re: Latency variance observed on Orchid integration - Model v11a

Hi Maria — thanks for the report and the samples. I've looped in our AE (Laura), CS/ops (Tessa) and eng (Rishi).

We can move quickly here. Two quick asks: can you confirm the exact subset of requests impacted (customer_id or endpoint path) and whether this is affecting both EU and US traffic or EU only? Also confirming SR-18732 is the ticket we'll use.

Operationally we can do a temporary traffic split (suggested: 30% -> v11a-compact) or trigger a controlled rollback of the v11a rollout. I want to get ops and eng alignment before touching customer traffic.

If you’re OK with the 30% split I can request authorization internally and start the change window immediately once we have sign-off.

—Logan

Team — forwarding the customer samples (attached) and details:
- Account: Orchid Labs (deal ORCH-2027-0023)
- Region: eu-west only
- Endpoint: /api/v1/infer/checkout
- Customer SLO: p95 < 400ms; current observed ~820ms in customer samples
- Support ticket: SR-18732 (attached)

Proposed mitigations:
1) Immediate: enable 30% traffic split to v11a-compact (quantized variant) for eu-west.
2) Short-term: enable KV cache prefill and prefix caching for this route.
3) If continued regression: controlled rollback of v11a rollout to previous stable variant.

Please confirm capacity on the dedicated pool for the fallover variant (Tessa) and whether ops can enact the split now. Rishi/Karthik, please advise if there are any compile/warmup steps we must run first; this is high-priority — customer has escalated.

I am asking for a temporary SLA carveout for p95 for up to 48 hours while we monitor the impact of the split; customer has agreed to that window if it helps stabilize.

Attachments: orchid_latency_samples_20271201.csv, support_ticket_SR-18732.pdf

—Logan
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-12-01T10:04:12Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: Orchid Labs (ORCH-2027-0023) — p95 spike on v11a (EU only) — request to activate 30% fallback and SLA carveout

Thanks Logan — quick triage notes: the pattern in the samples looks like cold KV cache behavior and a small but critical compile path divergence for long-context checkouts. Before we do a rollback, try the following short-term mitigations (safe to flip quickly):
- Enable KV cache prefill for the recent prefixes on the checkout route (this should reduce tail spikes shortly).
- Force the quantized v11a-compact variant to be eligible for prefix-based caching (low-risk).
- Reduce max batch size for this route from 32 -> 16 for eu-west to avoid long queuing under burst (we can revert in 1-2 hours).

Operationally I authorize the 30% traffic split to v11a-compact if ops confirms node capacity. If prefill + batch change removes the tail spike we can hold and avoid rollback. If not, we should prepare a controlled rollback plan (playbook in runbook_traffic_split.md) and notify customer.

Please collect: server-side traces for the affected requests, model compilation logs from the last deployment (model v11a build id), and the node eviction metrics. Send me the traces and logs (redwood internal link or attach).

—Rishi
Director, Inference Platform
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
